title: Mass fish kill wipes out 34 cages in Laguna de Bay off Jala-jala
summary: A fish kill that began on a Thursday in late August 2026 hit about 34 fish cages covering 6.4 hectares of Laguna de Bay off Jala-jala, Rizal, killing tilapia, bighead carp, kanduli, bangus and fingerlings. The fisherfolk group Pamalakaya put the loss at more than 20,000 kilograms of tilapia and bighead carp worth an estimated P700,000, and operators said the lake water had turned rusty in colour before the fish died. The LLDA said Laguna de Bay was under a widespread algal bloom that heavy rain could worsen and that the incident needed thorough evaluation, while BFAR collected water and fish samples; authorities warned the public not to buy or eat the floating fish.
referredTo: Laguna Lake Development Authority and BFAR

timeline.note: LLDA warned that changes in weather and water conditions could trigger or intensify algal growth whose decomposition reduces oxygen and can kill fish.
Fish began dying in cages off Jala-jala, with operators noting the lake water had turned rusty before the fish died.
BFAR was examining water and fish samples from the affected area while the LLDA said the incident required thorough evaluation because of the widespread algal bloom.
Pamalakaya reported more than 20,000 kg of tilapia and bighead carp lost across more than 30 cages, with initial losses estimated at P700,000, and suspected chemical waste.

title: Manila Water pipeline flushing discharged into Laguna de Bay
summary: On 9 July 2026 Manila Water Company Inc. flushed and disinfected the new pipes of its East Bay Transmission Mains Phase 2 project and discharged the water into Laguna de Bay at Binangonan, Rizal. The LLDA said the company emailed a request for approval to its Office of the General Manager at 4:32 p.m. that day but proceeded without waiting for evaluation or clearance. In the same week residents of Talim Island reported an algal bloom, first spotted on 8 July, and dead shrimp and goby washing ashore; Pamalakaya later described a July fish kill in Binangonan following the release of wastewater by the concessionaire.

timeline.note: Fishers on Talim Island spotted an algal bloom and reported dead shrimp and biya washing ashore.

Manila Water carried out flushing and disinfection of its East Bay Transmission Mains Phase 2 pipeline and discharged into the lake at Binangonan, emailing the LLDA a request at 4:32 p.m. the same day.
The LLDA said the company proceeded with the flushing and discharge without waiting for its evaluation or clearance.

title: Magat Dam fish kill kills tilapia stocks, losses hit P120 million
summary: Tilapia raised in fish cages at Magat Dam began dying on 23 June 2026, with about 10 metric tons of tilapia lost in cages in Ramon and Cordon, Isabela, in the first days. BFAR attributed the deaths to low dissolved oxygen after El Niño-driven heat lowered the dam's water level, and on 6 July put total losses at P120 million: P100 million in Alfonso Lista, Ifugao and P20 million in Ramon, Isabela. Pamalakaya said more than 1,400 fisherfolk in Ramon alone were affected and asked BFAR for relief and livelihood support.
referredTo: BFAR Region II and Isabela Provincial Fishery Office

timeline.note: Fish mortality among caged tilapia at Magat Dam was first observed.
BFAR linked the deaths to the drop in the dam's water level and low oxygen, advised operators to harvest remaining fish, and the provincial fishery office planned free fingerlings.
BFAR director Nazario Briguera reported P120 million in losses, while Pamalakaya asked the bureau for relief and livelihood aid for over 1,400 fisherfolk in Ramon.

title: Red tide and fish kills hit Panguil Bay towns in Lanao del Norte
summary: Seawater discoloration and mass fish mortality in Panguil Bay prompted the Tubod, Lanao del Norte local government to convene an emergency meeting on 13 May 2026. On 16 May BFAR raised a red tide alert for the whole bay after laboratory tests confirmed heavy blooms of Gymnodinium and Pleurosigma plankton, and shellfish from Tangub City, Misamis Occidental tested positive for paralytic shellfish toxin. New fish kills were reported in the coastal towns of Baroy and Tubod at the end of May; BFAR Northern Mindanao director Edward Yasay said fish cages in the area may have contributed and advised the public not to eat dead fish or swim in discoloured water.

timeline.note: The LGU convened an emergency meeting over widespread water discoloration and mass fish mortality.
BFAR raised a red tide alert for Panguil Bay after tests verified blooms of Gymnodinium and Pleurosigma species.
BFAR reported new fish kills in Baroy and Tubod, noted fish cages may have contributed, and advised the public against eating dead fish or swimming in discoloured areas.

title: Grounded cargo vessel leaks oil onto Badoc shoreline
summary: The cargo vessel LCT MSCI 1, carrying gravel from Ilocos Norte to Calayan, Cagayan, made an emergency beaching off Barangay La Virgen Milagrosa, Badoc on 8 June 2026 after listing in rough seas. An oil-and-water mixture spread along about 15 metres of coastline and oil residues were reported in Barangay Dadalaquiten Norte, Sinait, Ilocos Sur; the Philippine Coast Guard laid spill booms and absorbent pads with the BFP, PNP and Marine Battalion Landing Team-8. BFAR estimated three to five drums of oil mixture leaked within a 15-metre radius, recorded no fish kill, and said about 135 registered fisherfolk and 30 fishing vessels were affected, with DOLE cash-for-work and DSWD food aid arranged.
referredTo: Philippine Coast Guard and BFAR Region I

timeline.note: LCT MSCI 1 conducted an emergency beaching off Badoc after listing in rough seas.
PCG installed spill booms and absorbent pads along the coast while the DA and BFAR dispatched teams and arranged TUPAD and DSWD assistance for fishers.
BFAR said the estimated three to five drums of oil mixture were contained and no fish kill, abnormal fish behaviour or contaminated fishery products had been recorded.

title: Tugboat with 15,000 litres of diesel sinks off Botolan
summary: The tugboat SL Sual 1, owned by SMC Shipping and Lighterage Corporation, ran aground near the mouth of the Bucao River in Botolan, Zambales on 14 August 2026 and sank on 24 August while being towed during an emergency salvage operation, settling about 200 metres from shore in roughly 24 metres of water with about 15,000 litres of diesel aboard. Ten salvage workers jumped overboard and were rescued. The Philippine Coast Guard positioned absorbent pads and oil spill response equipment, ran shoreline patrols along the Bucao River, and reported the fuel tanks intact with no oil sheen observed.

timeline.note: The tugboat listed and ran aground near the Bucao River mouth after strong waves and seawater entered the vessel.
The tug sank at 7:46 a.m. during towing; PCG rescued 10 workers, staged spill response equipment and patrolled the shoreline, finding no sheen and intact fuel tanks.

title: URC distillery wastewater spill kills corals across Bais Bay
summary: A containment lagoon at Universal Robina Corporation's Bais Distillery collapsed on 26 October 2025, releasing about 255,000 cubic metres of spent wash into North Bais Bay and the Tañon Strait Protected Seascape, discolouring seawater and killing fish across ten coastal barangays. DENR-EMB Negros Island Region issued an interim cease-and-desist order on 27 October, the DENR filed complaints before the Bais City prosecutor, and the distillery remained suspended pending a Pollution Adjudication Board decision as of December 2025. A Silliman University survey presented on 7 July 2026 found 69 percent of surveyed corals recently dead, 4,494 to 6,000 hectares of waters affected and fish kills up to seven kilometres from the source, with a fishing ban still in place and fishers reporting continued discharge.
referredTo: DENR-EMB Negros Island Region and the Pollution Adjudication Board

timeline.note: Lagoon 6 of the ethanol distillery released most of its spent wash into North Bais Bay, with discoloured water and dead fish observed and a stop-operations order issued.
EMB issued an interim cease-and-desist order against URC Bais Distillery.
Operations stayed suspended while the PAB reviewed URC's appeal and the city prosecutor conducted preliminary investigation of charges including violation of the Expanded NIPAS Act.

title: Bulk water intake on Caliban River halted for permit violations
summary: DENR-EMB Negros Island Region issued a cease-and-desist order against Bacolod Bulk Water Inc.'s Bacolod-Murcia Sum-Ag Water Treatment Plant and its Caliban River water intake facility in Murcia, Negros Occidental, after residents of Barangay Caliban petitioned against the project. The company expanded its Water Supply Injection 2 project from a permitted 100 cubic metres per day to an additional 300 cubic metres per day without an amended Environmental Compliance Certificate, and had no discharge permit or permit to operate for its pollution source equipment. Residents complained the water they were receiving was dark, smelly and contaminated and feared the river would be depleted; EMB imposed a P70,000 fine and ordered operations stopped until the amended ECC is approved.

timeline.note: EMB issued a cease-and-desist order and P70,000 fine against BBWI for operating the plant and Caliban intake without a discharge permit, permit to operate and amended ECC.

The order directed BBWI to stop its Water Supply Injection 2 expansion at the Caliban River intake until its amended ECC application is approved, following complaints by Barangay Caliban and downstream residents.

title: Grease slick fouls Iloilo River along Diversion Road
summary: A thick layer of grease, locally called sebo, was found floating on the Iloilo River along Diversion Road in the Mandurriao district of Iloilo City in late July 2026. The City Environment and Natural Resources Office issued an office order creating a Joint Inspection Team to make random inspections of establishments near the affected stretch, collected samples of the grease and sent them to a laboratory for analysis of chemicals and pollutants. CENRO head Engr. Niel Ravena said violators face fines of up to P50,000 and suspension or revocation of permits.
referredTo: Iloilo City Environment and Natural Resources Office

timeline.note: CENRO formed a Joint Inspection Team to inspect nearby establishments' wastewater facilities and sent grease samples for laboratory analysis.
